doc.title: Lonnie Liston Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 9, 2021

title: World crisis and the message of his songs
summary: Fans revisit his peace songs written during Vietnam; he reacts to the January 6 events and to globalization.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: Bringing us up to current times, do you have any thoughts about why not only our country but the world seems to be in such crisis?

That’s the good part about — that’s, because I’m getting a lot of, what is it, FaceBook and Instagram and people saying all over the world now they’re revisiting a lot of those songs I wrote, you know, “Give Peace a Chance” and “Expansions” and I think “A

Garden of Peace.” That was the reason I wrote all those songs because back then we had the Vietnam war and all that, and a lot of other craziness. But now, and like I said, last Wednesday, I don’t know what they’re going to do about that, Monk, because you can’t take things that far. And the whole world saw it. I mean that went over the whole world on TV and — because people don’t realize now that what you call it — the cable and — when we go overseas we’re watching the same shows as if we’re at home. And then you can go online and it’s just like you being at home. I can be in Japan or Europe and so the world is that small now. So I just hope people realize that if we don’t work together, you know, we’re going to destroy each other and destroy the whole world. Because I mean at one time in America, America was the greatest so far as everything was manufactured in America and things were created here. But now, I listened this morning, they were saying they made a deal, they’re shipping things to other countries to be made and shipped back to America. So I think we have a lot to work on.
Could you have written a song like “A Garden of Peace” if you were in turmoil? If your spirit was not at peace? If you weren’t at peace yourself?
